text: The Patriots limp into Week 4 at Buffalo sporting a dismal 1-2 record and an offense that ranks dead last in the NFL at 9.7 points per game—a reality that's prompted considerable soul-searching from Drake Maye himself, who acknowledged his own play and the entire offensive unit's performance as "unacceptable" following Sunday's 35-6 shellacking by Jacksonville, though he insisted Wednesday that his right shoulder remains physically sound and hasn't impacted his throwing ability, suggesting the problems run deeper than injury. The roster situation hasn't helped matters: the Patriots placed guard Greg Van Roten on injured reserve Tuesday due to a thigh injury, forcing them to shore up the offensive line by signing rookie OL Da'Metrius Weatherspoon to the practice squad in a bid to stabilize the infrastructure protecting their young quarterback. Questions are swirling about whether the Patriots are deploying Maye incorrectly and whether he and his supporting cast can course-correct against the Bills at the new Highmark Stadium on Sunday, a game that appears increasingly critical to avoiding a catastrophic start to what was supposed to be a competitive season.
